headline: Highest risk is medium: Mentat’s filesystem writes and broad egress can conflict with the other agent’s shared-workspace assumptions, while prompt-injection and compliance risks are limited by the second agent’s lack of documented I/O.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat can read files and apply diff-based edits, so if spring-integration-samples’ outputs are manually copied into files, malicious instructions could be introduced. The pair has no documented direct channel, and the second agent exposes no I/O surfaces, so the pathway is indirect and low blast radius.
conditions: IF outputs from spring-integration-samples are copied into files that Mentat reads as task context
IF the operator treats copied text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Use a separate scratch file for copied text
Prefix copied content with provenance labels
Review file contents before Mentat processes them
Avoid pasting untrusted text into task prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat touches source code files and has broad network egress, but spring-integration-samples has no documented data classes or I/O surfaces. With no shared workspace or sensitive data class shown for B, leakage is possible only through unusual operator setup, so the blast radius is small and uncertain.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem workspace
IF sensitive source files are placed in that workspace and Mentat is allowed to transmit them
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate directories
Do not place secrets in shared workspaces
Disable network access for Mentat during sensitive tasks
Review outbound requests before enabling egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model explicitly shares state via filesystem. The second agent has no documented write controls, but the shared-workspace pathway is enough to create overwrite or git-state conflicts in default coding setups, so uncertainty does not justify lowering severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same working tree
IF either agent writes or commits without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize edits with a lock file
Require manual git review before commit
Run one agent at a time on shared repos

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals that a human or downstream workflow may apply, while spring-integration-samples is a repository-style artifact with no verification controls documented. If B consumes A’s outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect edits or actions; the interaction is plausible even though B’s runtime behavior is sparse.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples output is used as input to a downstream action or editor
IF no human verification step checks Mentat’s proposed diffs
mitigations: Require human approval for every diff
Add a verification checklist before applying outputs
Compare proposed changes against source files
Reject outputs lacking explicit provenance

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat handles model-provider API keys and broad egress, which can create policy issues if regulated source code is present. spring-integration-samples is open-source and shows no special residency or regulated-data handling, so there is no documented cross-border or PHI mismatch; the remaining concern is limited to local handling gaps.
conditions: IF regulated or proprietary code is placed into Mentat’s workspace
IF organizational policy forbids sending that code to a model provider
mitigations: Exclude regulated files from the workspace
Confirm retention policy for model-provider calls
Use a local-only model for sensitive code
Document data-handling rules for operators
